name: Seatbelt - Windows Host Situational Awareness
description: Seatbelt is a C# tool that gathers Windows "safety checks" for situational awareness from both offensive and defensive perspectives: tokens, UAC, LAPS, LSA settings, credential files, browser data, RDP sessions, PowerShell history, WEF/Sysmon config, AV/EDR presence, and more. Complements WinPEAS with cleaner, grouped, EDR-aware host triage.
notes:
=== RUN ALL CHECKS ===
  Seatbelt.exe -group=all
  Seatbelt.exe -group=all -full       # no truncation
  Seatbelt.exe -group=all -outputfile="C:\Windows\Temp\sb.txt"

=== CHECK GROUPS ===
  Seatbelt.exe -group=user      # user context, creds, history
  Seatbelt.exe -group=system    # system config, patches, services
  Seatbelt.exe -group=remote    # remote/network (run before pivoting)
  Seatbelt.exe -group=slack     # Slack/Teams creds
  Seatbelt.exe -group=chromium  # browser data

=== SPECIFIC CHECKS ===
  Seatbelt.exe TokenPrivileges UAC LAPS LSASettings
  Seatbelt.exe WindowsCredentialFiles CloudCredentials
  Seatbelt.exe PowerShellHistory PuttySessions
  Seatbelt.exe DotNet AMSIProviders Sysmon WindowsDefender   # evasion recon

=== DEFENSIVE / BLUE USE ===
  # Quickly audit a host for exposed creds + logging gaps
  Seatbelt.exe -group=all -full

=== ALTERNATIVES ===
  WinPEAS      # broader privesc focus
  PrivescCheck # PowerShell
  SharpUp      # service misconfig exploitation

examples.label: All checks, full output to file

recommended.note: WinPEAS for broader privesc vector coverage.
PrivescCheck is a stealthier PowerShell option.

defense.why_it_works: Seatbelt reads local configuration and credential-store locations via standard APIs. As a GhostPack C# tool it is often flagged by EDR, but unobfuscated reads of config/cred files succeed where not blocked.
defense.prerequisites: Shell on the target; .NET runtime; Seatbelt binary (or in-memory via C2).
defense.impact: Reveals stored credentials, privilege/UAC posture, and (critically) the host logging/EDR configuration enabling further evasion.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1082/T1518.001] Seatbelt binary/assembly signatures; reads of PowerShell history, PuTTY/WinSCP registry, browser cred stores; queries of Sysmon/Defender/AMSI configuration.
defense.artifacts: Seatbelt.exe or in-memory .NET assembly load (4104/CLR ETW); access to ConsoleHost_history.txt, cred vaults, AV config keys.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=windows EventCode=4688 (NewProcessName="*Seatbelt*" OR CommandLine="*-group=all*")
| table _time, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine
defense.sentinel_kql:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FileName has "Seatbelt" or ProcessCommandLine has "-group=all"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
defense.prevention: Credential Guard; remove stored plaintext creds (PuTTY/WinSCP/cloud CLI); enable AMSI + script block logging (so in-memory loads are caught); EDR signatures for GhostPack; restrict .NET where feasible.

detections.name: Seatbelt host enumeration
detections.logic:
union DeviceProcessEvents, DeviceEvents
| where FileName has "Seatbelt" or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("-group=all","AMSIProviders","LSASettings")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
detections.tuning: Also detect in-memory execution via Script Block / CLR ETW when run through C2
